LESSON: LAUNDRY WORK

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: HOME SCIENCE
Strand: Home Management
Topic 2.5: Laundry work
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Laundry work, part of Home Management in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 HOME SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we require laundry agents and detergents during laundry work? 2. Why is laundry work important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. classify detergents and agents used in laundry work,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Laundry work in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe tools and equipment used in laundry work,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Laundry work in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain the processes used in laundry work,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Laundry work in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. launder personal items following correct procedures,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Laundry work in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. embrace the importance of laundry work in day to-day-life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Laundry work in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. classify detergents and agents used in laundry work,

   Laundry work helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. describe tools and equipment used in laundry work,

   Laundry work helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. explain the processes used in laundry work,

   Laundry work helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. launder personal items following correct procedures,

   Laundry work helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. embrace the importance of laundry work in day to-day-life.

   Laundry work helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search for information and classify laundry detergents (soaps and soapless detergents) and agents (water - soft and hard, fabric conditioners, bleaches, stain removers, stiffeners, laundry blue, organic solvents). Learners with manipulation difficulties could be provided with adapted digital resources with appropriate accessibility features or be supported and make notes,

2. observe pictures or watch video clips and discuss the use of laundry work tools and equipment (classification, choice, use, care, safety precautions). Learners with 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search for information and classify laundry detergents (soaps and soapless detergents) and agents (water - soft and hard, fabric conditioners, bleaches, stain removers, stiffeners, laundry blue, organic solvents). Learners with manipulation difficulties could be provided with adapted digital resources with appropriate accessibility features or be supported and make notes,
2. observe pictures or watch video clips and discuss the use of laundry work tools and equipment (classification, choice, use, care, safety precautions). Learners with 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Laundry work together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: The learner practises the use and care of laundry work tools and equipment.

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The learner explores different options that may result in effective laundry work.

Values:
● Peace: Learners display tolerance by respecting other learner’s opinions when discussing the use of laundry work tools

and equipment.

● Responsibility: The learner engages in assigned roles and practises the use and care for tools and equipment used in

laundry work.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: The learner observes safety precautions when practising the use and care of laundry work tools and equipment

Suggested learning resources:

Adapted digital devices and print reference materials, general accessible environment for space/rooms to carry out cleaning,

selected adapted cleaning tools and equipment, first aid kit, laundry detergents and agents

Main points to remember:

1. classify detergents and agents used in laundry work,
2. describe tools and equipment used in laundry work,
3. explain the processes used in laundry work,
4. launder personal items following correct procedures,
5. embrace the importance of laundry work in day to-day-life.
